title: Discrete modules for a topological group have functorial injective embeddings
statement: Let $G$ be a topological group and $R$ a ring. In the category of left $R$-modules with a $G$-action by $R$-linear automorphisms such that every element has open stabilizer, and with $R$-linear $G$-equivariant maps, there is a functor $J$ and a natural transformation $j:\operatorname{id}\to J$ such that every $j_M:M\to J(M)$ is a monomorphism and every $J(M)$ is an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] in this category.

proof.text: For the group ring $R[G]$, the category of left modules has functorial injective embeddings by [lem-exc-rg-group-algebra-functorial-injective-embeddings].

source.place: Section G-modules, paragraph immediately before Tag 04JF

proof.text: The category of $R$-modules with a $G$-action whose elements have open stabilizer is related to the group-ring module category by the fully faithful mono-preserving forgetful functor and its right adjoint given by the open-stabilizer submodule, as stated in [lem-exc-rg-open-stabilizer-adjoint].

source.place: Tag 04JF, proof of lemma-G-modules, definition of v and u

proof.text: Applying the adjoint transfer lemma [lem-exc-rg-adjoint-transfer-functorial-injectives] to the data in steps 1 and 2 gives a functor $J$ on the open-stabilizer category, a natural transformation $j:\operatorname{id}\to J$ whose components are monomorphisms, and injective objects $J(M)$. This is the asserted functorial injective embedding.
